query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Put both files in `/etc/systemd/system/`. That is where systemd reads system-wide units, and the timer runs as root because the service has no `User=` line. On this workstation, `/etc` changes start in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/`, so keep a copy there and install it from there.

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.service`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup
After=local-fs.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup
```

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.timer`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly-backup every night at 02:00 local time

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

`OnCalendar` is read in the system's local time zone. `Persistent=true` makes systemd run a missed backup at the next boot, so a machine that was off at 02:00 still gets a backup that night. The timer activates `nightly-backup.service` because the names match, so no `Unit=` line is needed.

To install and start it:

1. `sudo -A systemctl daemon-reload`
2. `sudo -A systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer`
3. Check the next run with `systemctl list-timers nightly-backup.timer`.

If the backup should run as your user instead of root, add `User=glw907` under `[Service]`, and make sure that user can write to the backup destination.

I have not installed these files or enabled the timer. Say the word and I'll place the copies in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/`, install them, and run the enable step.
